claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Pack cementation at approximately 900 °C for 4–8 hours in an aluminum-rich packing mixture can deposit a thin, uniform aluminide coating on the as-cast alloy.
An aluminide surface coating will improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at around 1000 °C.
The aluminide coating will develop a continuous and adherent Al2O3 overlayer during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminide layer acts as an aluminum reservoir from which aluminum diffuses outward during high-temperature exposure.
Outward-diffusing aluminum forms a dense, slow-growing Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The oxygen diffusion barrier mitigates further internal oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating and oxidation treatment will not alter the alloy's bulk microstructure.
The aluminide-coated alloy will have a lower oxidation rate than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours.
The aluminide-coated alloy will show minimal mass gain during high-temperature oxidation exposure.
After coating and exposure, the alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
After coating and exposure, the alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to that of the untreated alloy at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation in oxygen-containing high-temperature environments and consequently degrades in performance.
Coating-substrate interdiffusion, inadequate scale adhesion, or coating-induced brittleness under cyclic loading may compromise performance.
